meta.title: The Best Dhikr App for iPhone in 2026 (Ranked)
meta.description: We ranked the best dhikr app for iPhone in 2026. QuranWall tops it — keeping the remembrance of Allah on your lock screen all day.

sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: The best dhikr app for iPhone in 2026 is QuranWall, if you want remembrance in front of you without opening anything. It puts an ayah on your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or a translation. It is not a tasbih counter, so Muslim Pro or Pillars can sit beside it for counting.

sections.text: Most people searching for the **best dhikr app for iPhone** want the same thing: to remember Allah more often, not just when they remember to open an app. That last part is the trap. A tasbih counter is only as good as your discipline in launching it — and by week two, the icon sits untouched on page three of your home screen. The apps below are ranked by one question: how well do they keep the remembrance of Allah present in your actual day?
What a dhikr app really needs to do

Dhikr means remembrance. So the job isn't counting — counting is the easy part your thumb can do. The hard part is being reminded to start. A great dhikr app has to close the gap between intention and action: it should surface remembrance where you already look, hold a morning-and-evening rhythm, and never demand that you dig through folders to begin. Judge every app on that, and the ranking sorts itself out fast.

sections.content: **1. QuranWall — best for keeping dhikr in front of you (Editor's pick)**

sections.text: QuranWall wins because it solves the reminder problem instead of the counting one. It places an ayah of the Quran directly on your **iPhone lock screen** wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or a translation, and the ayah stays put until you pick another in the app. Every time you pick up your phone, a verse is already there. No streak to babysit. You choose the background, font and colours, so the screen can suit your prayer or evening wind-down. For turning remembrance into something you *see* rather than something you have to schedule, it is the most direct fit on this list. That's why it ranks first as the **best dhikr app for iPhone** in 2026 — with one caveat: QuranWall shows Quran verses, it is not a tasbih counter.

sections.content: On iOS 16 or later, iOS can link a Lock Screen to a Focus (touch and hold the Lock Screen, then tap Focus). Link the one with your ayah to a Focus you run after Maghrib, and the Lock Screen becomes your cue for evening adhkar without a single notification.

sections.text: If you want the full lock-screen walkthrough, we cover it in [how to set dhikr reminders on iPhone](/blog/how-to-set-dhikr-reminders-iphone), and QuranWall also topped our [best Islamic lock screen app roundup](/blog/best-islamic-lock-screen-app-iphone).

sections.content: **2. Muslim Pro — best all-in-one with a built-in tasbih**

sections.text: Muslim Pro bundles prayer times, qibla, a Quran reader, and a digital tasbeeh counter into one app. If you want a single install that does a bit of everything and you're happy to open it deliberately, it's a reasonable pick. Its dhikr feature is a counter, though — it waits for you to launch it. It solves a different, broader job than QuranWall's daily-exposure lane, so it sits below the top spot for pure remembrance.

sections.content: **3. Pillars — best for adhkar as a daily checklist**

sections.text: Pillars leans into habit-building: prayer tracking with a clean design and space for daily worship goals. If you think in checklists and want to log morning and evening adhkar as tasks, it fits. But a checklist still lives inside the app — you have to go to it. It complements QuranWall rather than replacing a verse on your lock screen.

sections.content: **4. Athan by IslamicFinder — best if you mainly want prayer alerts**

sections.text: Athan is built around accurate adhan times and includes some dua content. It's dependable for the salah schedule, and prayer is the anchor dhikr sits around. But it's a prayer-times app first; remembrance is a side feature, not the surface. Keep it for the adhan, lead with QuranWall for the dhikr.

Here's the part nobody tells you about tasbih apps: **the rotation dies by week two.** Opening a counter is a habit, and habits that depend on you remembering to launch something fade fast. The same goes for screenshotting a verse and setting it as your wallpaper — you'll do it twice, then forget. QuranWall sidesteps both by designing the ayah for the surface you can't ignore, and changing it takes a few taps in the app. You don't need discipline to *look at your own lock screen* — you already do it all day.

sections.label: translation languages
sections.description: QuranWall shows each ayah in Uthmani Arabic or in a translation, and you can choose from 10 languages.

sections.text: Read the ayah in Uthmani Arabic or in a translation in the language you think in, and the verse lands. Whichever you choose, the highest-leverage place for remembrance isn't inside an app you open twice — it's the screen you glance at all day. The Quran ties that assurance directly to remembrance.
Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.

items: Download QuranWall from the App Store.
Choose your translation language, then a background, font and colours — a preset or your own photo.
Put the ayah on your Lock Screen wallpaper and add the widget to your Home Screen.
Optional: attach that lock screen to an iOS Focus mode for prayer or evening.
Then leave it on your Lock Screen — remembrance every time you look. Turn on auto-rotate and the widget shows a new ayah every day.

sections.content: A dhikr counter counts what you already remembered to do. A lock-screen verse reminds you in the first place. For most people, the reminder is the missing piece — not the counter.

sections.text: So rank them honestly: keep a tasbih counter if you love logging reps, keep Athan for the adhan, and for weaving remembrance into a fuller day see our [Muslim morning routine setup](/blog/muslim-morning-routine-iphone). For the wider picture, see our [best Muslim app for iPhone](/blog/best-muslim-app-for-iphone-2026) ranking. But the app that makes dhikr happen without effort — the one that puts the remembrance of Allah where you actually are — is QuranWall.
